General information: Process Title: New Employee Onboarding. Department: Human Resources. Contact Info: HR Department - hr@acmetech.com | +1 (555) 123-4567. SOP ID: HR-SOP-001. Effective Date: 2026-05-17. Revision Number: 1.0. Process overview: Process Description: This procedure defines the standardized process for onboarding new employees, covering pre-start activities, first-day orientation, system and facility provisioning, training assignments, and milestone reviews through confirmation of employment. Purpose & Scope: Purpose: Ensure a consistent, compliant, and positive onboarding experience for all new hires. Scope: Applies to all full-time, part-time, and contract hires across all Acme Tech Solutions locations. Covers HR, IT, Facilities, Payroll, Hiring Managers, and Training teams. Definitions and related documents: Definitions: 'New Hire' - individual with accepted employment offer; 'HRIS' - Human Resources Information System; 'Onboarding Checklist' - standardized list of tasks to complete for each new hire. Related Documents: Offer Letter Template, Employee Handbook, Background Check Policy, I-9 and Tax Forms, HRIS User Guide, IT Account Provisioning Guide, Facilities Access Request Form. Owner: HR Business Partner. WBS 2.6 — Conduct 60-day development review and adjust goals or support as needed. Owner: Hiring Manager & HR Business Partner. WBS 2.7 — Conduct 90-day probationary review and confirm employment status or recommend actions. Owner: HR Manager. HTML:

1.9 Provision IT accounts, email, and necessary system access IT Department
1.10 Prepare workspace, security badge and physical access Facilities
1.11 Conduct first-day orientation and company overview HR
Purpose &Scope 1.12 Deliver role-specific training plan and resources Training Department
Purpose: To deliver a consistent, compliant, and positive onboarding experience that enables new employees to become productive quickly. Scope: Applies to all full-time, part-time, and fixed-term employees across all company locations. 1.13 Manager meets new hire to set expectations and goals Hiring Manager

When complete bring this form with you and turn it in to the program coordinator. Please clearly denote the required vaccinations if you are including multiple health forms. Copy of a current American Heart Association or American Red Cross Basic Life Support for Healthcare Provider card (signed-copy front and back of card). — JD 2. UCLA Center for Prehospital Care
Prerequisite Medical Requirements for EMT Students
Welcome and thank you for your interest in the UCLA Center for Prehospital Care EMT Program! This information is provided to help you meet the documentation and medical requirements for the EMT program. These requirements are developed by the Department of Health and Human Services and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. In addition to needing the below medical requirements for your EMT program, our clinical/field affiliates will require the same immunizations in order for you to participate in their program.
Medical Services
Your physician's office should be able to provide everything you need to complete your EMT program prerequisites. Physician's offices and pharmacies (such as CVS) that have walk up services may also be able to complete the health requirements. For other locations in Los Angeles County please visit the Department of Health Services web site at: www.ladhs.org/clinics/.
Name: Student ID: Course #:
The following items are required to complete the ride along portion of the EMT course. The ride alongs must be completed within 30 days of the end of the course so it is important to complete this documentation as soon as possible. When complete bring this form with you and turn it in to the program coordinator. Please clearly denote the required vaccinations if you are including multiple health forms.
Student Requirements Coordinator Initials (for office use)
1. Copy of a current American Heart Association or American Red Cross Basic Life Support for Healthcare Provider card (signed-copy front and back of card).
2. Proof of health insurance coverage including private insurer, or state provided insurance, or federal provided insurance (copy front and back of card).
3. Proof of Hepatitis B Vaccine or refusal as demonstrated on the Hepatitis Verification Form.
4. Completion of the Flu Vaccine Requirement form.
5. Proof of current Measles/Mumps/Rubella (MMR) immunization or titer.
6. Proof of current Tetanus/Diphtheria/Pertussis (Tdap) immunization or titer.
7. Proof of current varicella (chicken pox or VZV) immunization, or titer, or a signed and dated note from a physician indicating you have had the chicken pox.
8. Proof of negative TB skin test (within 3 months), or Quantiferon-Gold blood test (within 3 months), or a negative chest x-ray (within 2 years).
9. Original Physical and Mask Fit Clearance form, found in this packet, stamped or signed and dated from a physician within 6 months prior to the start of class specifying that you can participate in the clinical portion of the EMT program without physical limitations.
10. Proof of COVID19 Vaccination. While the vaccine may not be required for your specific course, if you have received vaccination, please include a copy.

Relevant information: Background: This document is an application for registration as a scheme operator under the Factories and Industrial Undertakings (Safety Management) Regulation, submitted using the approved form specified by the Commissioner for Labour. It sets out the applicant’s particulars, full particulars of the proposed training scheme, detailed scheme contents, trainer credentials, other relevant information, and the required declaration and authorizing signature. Particulars of the applicant: The name in English is ABC Safety Training Limited and the name in Chinese characters is 安保培訓有限公司. The nature of the applicant is Company. The Identity Card/Passport/Business Registration/Company Registration Number is 12345678. The address is Unit 10B, 12/F, Industrial Building, 88 Factory Road, Kowloon, Hong Kong. The responsible person is Chan Tai-man, whose post is Managing Director, and the telephone number is +852 2345 6789. Particulars of the scheme: The training scheme title is Workplace Safety Management Certification. The scheme duration is 4 weeks (16 sessions). The contact hours total 40 hours. The certificate to be issued is the Certificate of Completion in Safety Management. Assessment of the trainee is divided between Homework/Continuous Assessment, which constitutes 40%, and Test & Examination, which constitutes 60%. Facilities provided include a lecture room with projector, whiteboard, PPE for demonstrations (helmets, gloves, harness), a first-aid kit, and training mannequins. Details of the scheme: Scheme contents cover introduction to relevant legislation, hazard identification, risk assessment, control measures, emergency procedures, permit-to-work systems and practical workshops including case studies and site inspections. Particulars of trainers: - Lee Wai-ming, R123456(7); academic qualifications BEng (Safety Engineering) and MPhil (Occupational Safety); 10 years in workplace safety training, consultancy and risk assessment. - Chan Siu-ling, S234567(8); academic qualifications BSc (Occupational Safety and Health) and Certified Trainer; 8 years conducting safety management and compliance training for industrial clients. - Wong Ho, E12345678 (Passport); academic qualification Diploma in Industrial Safety; 5 years as industry safety officer and practical workshop facilitator. - Ng Shek, T345678(9); academic qualification MSc (Risk Management); 12 years as safety manager and trainer in manufacturing and construction sectors. - Tam Mei-ling, P987654(3); academic qualification BSc (Environmental Health and Safety); 7 years delivering safety audits, incident investigation and emergency response training. Other relevant information: Training materials, attendance records and assessment results will be retained for 5 years. The maximum class size is 30 participants. Practical sessions will be conducted with appropriate safety supervision. Declaration and signature: The applicant declares that the particulars contained in the form and the attached information are true and correct to the best of their knowledge and belief, and understands that registration obtained by fraud or on the basis of inaccurate or misleading information is liable to cancellation under section 29(2)(b) of the aforesaid Regulation. A set of related information is enclosed with the application. The chop of the organisation is to be affixed. The authorized signatory is Chan Tai-man. Name: Chan Tai-man. Relevant information: Part I: To Licensing Authority, Venue Safety Department. This application concerns the use of laser effects at the venue Esplanade - Theatres on the Bay, Concert Hall for the event Summer Music Festival - Evening Concert Series. Performance dates are 15 July 2026 - 17 July 2026, occurring on days 15, 16, 17 in the month of July in the year 2026, with a total number of performances of 3. Opening Act - Band A is scheduled from 20:00 to 20:05 (5 minutes). The laser product to be used is a Laserworld CS-2000RGB. The planned display is a stage wash and aerial beam patterns above the stage, with no audience scanning. Safety measures: beams will be confined to the stage and overhead; interlocks and key switch enabled; the operator will perform a pre-show safety sweep; audience scanning is disabled; beam paths will be verified for safe divergence and elevation. Mid Set - DJ Performance is scheduled from 21:00 to 21:10 (10 minutes). The laser product to be used is an Elation KL Panel Q2. The planned display is graphic beam effects into the upper auditorium and stage backdrops, with low-angle silhouette beams on stage only. Safety measures: ILDA control limits will be applied; attenuation will be used for any beams angled toward seating; a trained operator will be onsite; visible beam path checks will be conducted and an operator emergency kill switch will be positioned front-of-house. Finale - Full Cast is scheduled from 22:30 to 22:35 (5 minutes). The laser system will be a Pangolin FB4 controller with KVANT ClubMAX 3000. The planned display is fast-moving aerial beams and strobes synchronized to music, limited to overhead and stage effects only. Safety measures: a dedicated safety officer with a kill switch will be at FOH; there will be no direct eye-level audience scanning; all reflective surfaces will be masked; the operator is certified for Class 4 operation; pre-show divergence and irradiance measurements will be logged. Note: 1. Do not look directly to the origin of laser beam. 2. No laser beam or its reflection shall be directed to persons (including audience, performers and operators liable to view the beam or its reflection). Signature: John Tan (signed). Part I: To Manager — To: Police Licensing Office. Venue: Grand Theatre, Cultural Centre. Performance dates: 2026-06-15 to 2026-06-20. Day(s): Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun. Mth(s): June. Yr(s): [no entry]. No. of Perf.: 6. Event: Evening Performances - "The Last Salute". Act I / Scene 2 is scheduled at 00:18:30 - 00:18:45 (15 seconds). The prop to be used is 1 prop pistol, serial no. M-001, with 1 blank shot. The action description and safety measures: the actor fires downward into a sand trap; blank ammunition only; the firearm will be inspected and cleared by the Firearms Management Specialist (FMS) before each performance; a safety officer will be positioned stage left with a fire extinguisher and first aid kit; and barriers will be used to keep the audience at a safe distance. Act II / Scene 1 is scheduled at 00:52:10 - 00:52:25 (15 seconds). The prop to be used is 1 revolver prop, serial no. M-002, with 2 blank shots. The action description and safety measures: the actor points the revolver away from the audience and blanks are fired into a ballistic sponge; the FMS supervises loading and ejection; the actor will wear ear protection when off-stage; and clear communication callouts are established between the stage manager and the safety officer. Act III / Scene 4 is scheduled at 01:20:00 - 01:20:10 (10 seconds). The prop to be used is 1 rifle replica, serial no. M-003, with 1 blank shot. The action description and safety measures: the rifle is fired into a sealed backstop by a trained performer; the range of fire is restricted and stage crew will clear the downstage area; the FMS performs a live safety check and documents the chain of custody; and no live primers or projectiles are used. Curtain Call (Safety Demonstration) is scheduled at 01:35:00 - 01:35:30 (30 seconds). The prop is 1 prop pistol, serial no. M-004, with 0 shots (demonstration only with unloaded prop). The action description and safety measures: an unloaded prop is presented to the audience for demonstration; the FMS verifies unloaded status onstage; the performer avoids pointing at the audience; and venue management and the FMS confirm post-performance secure storage. Exemption Permit No: EP-2026-045 and EP-2026-046. FMS: John Cheng, Firearms Management Specialist, License No. FMS-789. Relevant information: Background/context: This submission concerns a complaint against a telecommunications/broadcasting licensee alleging suspected contravention of the "fair trading sections" of the Trade Descriptions Ordinance (Cap. 362). The complainant reported alleged misleading advertising, failure to disclose contract terms, unexpected charges, and incorrect representation of contract duration. The telecommunications licensee named in the complaint is ABC Telecom Limited. The complainant has lodged the matter with another enforcement agency. The complaint was reported to the Customs and Excise Department on 2026-05-10, reference number CEX/2026/12345. The Department acknowledged receipt and opened a preliminary inquiry, requested supporting documents, and indicated further follow-up pending review. Details of the complaint: On 2026-04-15 the complainant visited an ABC Telecom retail outlet and was offered a promotional plan advertised as a "free handset with 12-month contract." The salesperson verbally confirmed a 12-month commitment and no upfront fees. After signing the contract on 2026-04-15, the complainant was charged a $200 activation fee and found that the written agreement placed them on a 24-month contract. The monthly fee shown in the advertisement ($98) does not match the $128 monthly fee on the contract. The complainant attempted to resolve the matter with the store and with customer service; they refused to amend the contract or refund the activation fee. The complainant believes ABC Telecom misrepresented the offer and failed to disclose key contract terms, potentially breaching the fair trading sections of the TDO. Documents and information provided with the complaint: a. Contracts: Yes. b. Bills (e.g. monthly statements): Yes. c. Prepaid cards and packages: No. d. Advertisements or leaflets: Yes. e. Records of correspondence: Yes. f. Identification documents of the salespersons involved: No. g. Recordings of conversations with the salespersons involved: Yes. h. Others: Screenshots of the online advertisement, chat transcripts with customer service, and the in-store receipt. HTML:

Relevant information: Background: Maple Community Food Bank, Charity Registration Number 123456789RR0001, is applying for a reduction to its disbursement quota for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026 (Year 2026). We request a reduction of $15,000 ($15000.00) for the 2026 fiscal year; attached calculations explain the amount specified and show the projected shortfall in available resources for qualifying expenditures due to unforeseen capital repairs and a drop in donations. Summary of circumstances: 1) Facility damage and repairs: on January 15, 2026, the charity’s primary warehouse and distribution centre sustained significant roof and structural damage following an ice-dam event. Emergency temporary repairs and safety remediation required closure of the distribution centre for six weeks, from January 16 to February 28, 2026. The total estimated repair cost is $60,000. Insurance coverage applies but there is a $10,000 deductible and an anticipated claims processing delay of 4–6 months; interim cash requirements have forced the charity to reallocate funds previously designated for qualifying program disbursements. 2) Temporary program suspension and reduced in-kind receipts: the closure resulted in suspension of two regular community meal programs and a large volunteer-run food distribution for four weeks, reducing qualifying disbursements (direct food distribution and program delivery) by an estimated $8,500 for the fiscal year. 3) Reduced donations and fundraising revenue: a local economic downturn and the timing of the closure coinciding with our major year-end campaign produced a 22% reduction in monetary donations relative to projections for the period November 2025–March 2026. This represents an estimated revenue shortfall of $12,000, part of which would normally have been directed to program disbursements during the fiscal year. Net impact and reduction sought: expected increases in non-program expenditures for repairs, temporary storage, and the insurance deductible amount to $10,000 (out-of-pocket) to be paid in the 2026 fiscal year. Estimated lost qualifying disbursements due to program suspension and reduced donations total $8,500, so the total net shortfall against planned qualifying disbursements is approximately $18,500. After applying available reserve reallocation and minor expense cuts totaling $3,500, the charity requires a reduction of $15,000 to the Disbursement Quota for the 2026 fiscal year to avoid depleting operating reserves and ensure continuity of essential services. Supporting documents submitted with this application include detailed repair invoices and contractor estimates dated January–March 2026; the insurance claim submission and correspondence indicating the deductible and processing timeline; monthly income and donation reports for November 2025–March 2026 showing the shortfall; and a calculation worksheet summarizing projected qualifying disbursements before and after the incident. The requested reduction is temporary for the specified taxation year and is required to allow the charity to complete necessary repairs, restore program capacity, and maintain solvency while awaiting insurance recovery and the return to normal donation levels. Relevant information: Background/context: This is the training and internship placement plan for the exchange visitor participating as a Trainee under the Global Exchange Program, Inc., program number GEP-2026-045. The placement is hosted at the BioHealth Research Center - Molecular Biology Division and involves a laboratory research rotation focused on molecular biology techniques and research practice. The exchange visitor is Nguyen, Thi An (Surname/Primary, Given Name(s) must match passport name). The Exchange Visitor is: Trainee. Program Sponsor: Global Exchange Program, Inc. Program Number: GEP-2026-045. The main program supervisor and point of contact at the host organization is Dr. Maria L. Alvarez. Supervisor contact information: Dr. Maria L. Alvarez, Senior Director, BioHealth Research Center; +1-202-555-0134; malvarez@biohealthcenter.org. Title: Senior Director, Research & Training. Phone: +1-202-555-0134; Fax: +1-202-555-0199. Email: malvarez@biohealthcenter.org. Phase information: Phase Site Name: BioHealth Research Center - Molecular Biology Division. Training/Internship Field: Molecular Biology Research (gene expression, protein interactions, assay development). Phase Site Address: 1201 Research Parkway, Suite 400, Bethesda, MD 20814, USA. Phase Name: Laboratory Research Internship - Rotation 1. Start Date (mm-dd-yyyy) of Phase: 07-01-2026. End Date (mm-dd-yyyy) of Phase: 12-31-2026. Phase 1 of 3. Primary phase supervisor: Dr. Samuel K. Peterson. Supervisor Title: Senior Research Scientist, Molecular Biology. E-mail: speterson@biohealthcenter.org. Phone Number: +1-202-555-0178. Description of Trainee/Intern's role for this program or phase: The trainee will participate in hands-on laboratory research focused on characterization of gene expression pathways and protein interaction networks. Responsibilities include performing molecular cloning, PCR/qPCR, Western blotting, immunoprecipitation assays, cell culture maintenance, preparation of reagents and buffers, data collection, data entry into laboratory information management systems, routine equipment calibration, and contributing to weekly lab meetings and progress reports. The trainee will also assist in troubleshooting experiments and maintaining laboratory notebooks in accordance with institutional standards. Specific goals and objectives for this program or phase: 1) Acquire proficiency in core molecular biology techniques (cloning, PCR/qPCR, Western blot, immunoprecipitation) and demonstrate accurate execution of at least five representative protocols by week 12. 2) Design and execute a small independent sub-project under supervision, including hypothesis generation, experimental planning, data collection, and preliminary analysis, resulting in a written interim report by week 20. 3) Develop competence in laboratory data management and interpretation, including use of LIMS and basic statistical analysis tools, demonstrated by proper documentation and presentation at the end-of-phase seminar. 4) Improve scientific communication skills through participation in weekly lab meetings and by delivering one oral presentation and one written summary of findings by phase end. Names and titles of those who will provide continuous (for example, daily) supervision of the Trainee/Intern, including the primary supervisor, and their qualifications to teach the planned learning: Primary supervisor: Dr. Samuel K. Peterson, Senior Research Scientist — PhD in Molecular Biology, 12 years experience leading protein interaction studies, principal investigator on multiple NIH-funded projects; provides daily bench supervision, protocol training, and experimental design mentoring. Co-supervisor: Dr. Aisha R. Khan, Postdoctoral Researcher — PhD in Biochemistry, expertise in qPCR and protein assays, will provide hands-on technique training and day-to-day troubleshooting. Lab Manager: Ms. Elena Gomez, Laboratory Manager — M.Sc. in Molecular Diagnostics, responsible for safety training, LIMS instruction, and ensuring adherence to SOPs. Each supervisor has documented mentoring experience and has led research trainees through experimental design, data analysis, and scientific communication; their combined expertise covers all planned techniques and objectives for the trainee. Relevant information: 研发活动编号为 RD-2013-001 的项目，研发活动名称为“高能量密度锂电池高效快充技术研发”，起止时间为 2013-01-01 至 2015-12-31。该项目所属技术领域为“电池与储能技术（锂离子电池快充与材料工程）”，技术来源为“企业自主研发并与高校合作联合攻关”，知识产权编号为 CN201410123456.7。项目研发经费总预算为 1200 万元，近三年研发经费总支出为 1200 万元，其中 2015 年支出 500 万元，2014 年支出 400 万元，2013 年支出 300 万元。 项目目的及组织实施方式为：本项目旨在突破锂离子电池在高倍率充电过程中的容量衰减和安全瓶颈，开发适用于电动汽车的高能量密度、支持快充的电池体系与配套管理系统。组织实施采取企业主导、产学研结合的模式：由企业牵头设立项目组，承担样品制造、工程化测试与产业化验证；与高校和科研院所签订合作协议，负责材料设计、机理研究与基础测试；并与第三方检测机构开展安全与可靠性评估。项目分阶段实施，包含材料筛选、电池单体优化、电池包与 BMS 开发、整车适配与示范运行，确保技术可量产并满足相关法规与标准。 核心技术及创新点包括：1) 阴极与负极材料协同设计：通过改性正极和纳米结构负极显著提升材料在高倍率下的结构稳定性和循环寿命；2) 快充专用电解液与添加剂配方：定制电解液降低界面阻抗并提升高温稳定性；3) 高性能隔膜及界面工程：采用涂层隔膜与表面处理技术抑制枝晶生长；4) 智能电池管理系统(BMS)：基于模型预测与在线状态估算实现动态充电路径优化，降低电池老化速率；5) 体系级热管理与安全策略：整合被动与主动热管理设计，结合故障诊断与安全断电策略，提升整体安全性。以上创新点在材料、器件与系统层面形成协同效应，实现快充与长寿命的技术平衡。 已取得的阶段性成果为：1) 工艺与样品：完成多批次正负极材料配方优化，制备出 500 多片性能稳定的电池单体样品；2) 性能指标：在 1C 至 5C 倍率循环测试中，样品保持 ≥85% 初始容量（经过 1000 次等效衰减推算达到行业目标寿命）；实现 30 分钟内达到 80% SOC 的快充能力；3) 知识产权：已申请并授权国内发明专利 1 项（号 CN201410123456.7），另有 2 项专利正在审查中；4) 系统验证：开发出集成 BMS 原型并完成电池包级热管理与安全测试，已通过第三方机构的过充、短路及针刺试验；5) 示范应用：完成车辆级小批量装配与路试验证，数据表明快充场景下热稳定性和 SOC 估算满足设计指标，为下一步产业化奠定基础。 HTML:

Relevant information: 研发活动编号为 RD-2013-001 的项目，研发活动名称为“高能量密度锂电池高效快充技术研发”，起止时间为 2013-01-01 至 2015-12-31。该项目所属技术领域为“电池与储能技术（锂离子电池快充与材料工程）”，技术来源为“企业自主研发并与高校合作联合攻关”，知识产权编号为 CN201410123456.7。项目研发经费总预算为 1200 万元，近三年研发经费总支出为 1200 万元，其中 2015 年支出 500 万元，2014 年支出 400 万元，2013 年支出 300 万元。 项目目的及组织实施方式为：本项目旨在突破锂离子电池在高倍率充电过程中的容量衰减和安全瓶颈，开发适用于电动汽车的高能量密度、支持快充的电池体系与配套管理系统。组织实施采取企业主导、产学研结合的模式：由企业牵头设立项目组，承担样品制造、工程化测试与产业化验证；与高校和科研院所签订合作协议，负责材料设计、机理研究与基础测试；并与第三方检测机构开展安全与可靠性评估。项目分阶段实施，包含材料筛选、电池单体优化、电池包与 BMS 开发、整车适配与示范运行，确保技术可量产并满足相关法规与标准。 核心技术及创新点包括：1) 阴极与负极材料协同设计：通过改性正极和纳米结构负极显著提升材料在高倍率下的结构稳定性和循环寿命；2) 快充专用电解液与添加剂配方：定制电解液降低界面阻抗并提升高温稳定性；3) 高性能隔膜及界面工程：采用涂层隔膜与表面处理技术抑制枝晶生长；4) 智能电池管理系统(BMS)：基于模型预测与在线状态估算实现动态充电路径优化，降低电池老化速率；5) 体系级热管理与安全策略：整合被动与主动热管理设计，结合故障诊断与安全断电策略，提升整体安全性。以上创新点在材料、器件与系统层面形成协同效应，实现快充与长寿命的技术平衡。 已取得的阶段性成果为：1) 工艺与样品：完成多批次正负极材料配方优化，制备出 500 多片性能稳定的电池单体样品；2) 性能指标：在 1C 至 5C 倍率循环测试中，样品保持 ≥85% 初始容量（经过 1000 次等效衰减推算达到行业目标寿命）；实现 30 分钟内达到 80% SOC 的快充能力；3) 知识产权：已申请并授权国内发明专利 1 项（号 CN201410123456.7），另有 2 项专利正在审查中；4) 系统验证：开发出集成 BMS 原型并完成电池包级热管理与安全测试，已通过第三方机构的过充、短路及针刺试验；5) 示范应用：完成车辆级小批量装配与路试验证，数据表明快充场景下热稳定性和 SOC 估算满足设计指标，为下一步产业化奠定基础。 HTML:
